claim_reviews.rationale: A bounded community practice of wave-model teaching is supported by original 1862 report and 2009/2016 ethnography. Capability classification and locational scope reflect documented evidence; do not infer origin or continuity.

Original Winkler p. 494 classifies mattang as a general teaching chart without particular islands and meddo and rebbelib by scope; p. 495 describes teaching and reminders. Gulick, Genz et al. and Genz document practice and learning.

Original p. 304 describes stick maps used to retain and impart knowledge of island directions and distances, with sticks representing currents or waves. June is publication date rather than invention; caveat preserves that distinction.

The scan cover dates English edition 1901; p. 487 identifies 1898 German original and Jaluit 1896, pp. 488–490 describe return and mediated inquiries with Lojak and Laumanuan, and pp. 494–496 give chart classes and abstract teaching example. Event date is publication, not invention; caveats preserve mediation.

Original Genz states Bokin conveyed concepts by weaving the meto in his sitting mat at Ujae; Joel had Eknilang’s wapepe in mind and WAM interview dates the voyage 2006. 2009 coauthors describe shore and canoe learning. The interval is the documented episode, not the practice’s invention.

Gulick is earliest dated account located here; its 1862 date is not invention. Winkler and Genz support the described distinct historical and recent models; a continuity question is warranted without claiming transmission.

Genz et al. dates fieldwork June 2005–September 2006 and describes demonstrations; Genz 2016 distinguishes an engine-assisted outbound leg from return using swell shadow and current cues; 2014 interview gives the year and route. Specific voyage extends existing demonstration record; 2005–2006 prior event is broader and does not separately specify route or return-leg result.

Retain as candidate question only. Both endpoints are explicit: Bokin taught Joel at Ujae before the return and Genz reports Joel had both models in mind and selected cues; this supports the proposed direction and context as a question. Genz and 2014 interview share lineage, so independent corroboration for establishing this consequential relation is absent. Do not draw as established history.

New wording distinguishes museum interpretation from documented use and collection from manufacture. This refines existing instance, not a duplicate of the community capability.
